 Judgment
The petitioners filed this petition U/Sec.166 of M.V. Act, 1989 claiming compensation of
Rs.50,00,000/- from respondents due to death of Ram Kumar Gurung in a road traffic accident.
2. Brief facts of

Petitioners case are that, on 04.10.2022 at about 1.30 p.m. the deceased Ram Kumar Gurung was proceeding as a co-driver in a Mahindra Tempo bearing Reg.No.KA-53/D-5269 at that time one Sanju Pariyar was driving the same in a rash and negligent manner endangering to human life, at high speed and dashed against the left side of Chinnaiah Reddy Wall Compound and caused the accident.
As a result the deceased's head struck in between the wall and Tempo and he sustained severe head injuries.
Immediately the injured was shifted to Vydehi Hospital, wherein the doctor declared he was died on the way to the hospital.
Thereafter dead body was shifted to mortuary for postmortem and handed over the body to the petitioners.

3. Prior to the date of accident deceased was hale, healthy and aged about 26 years and working as a driver under Ranganatha Gas Agencies at Bangalore and earning Rs.25,000/- per month and contributing his entire earnings to maintain the family.
Petitioner No.1 is the wife, petitioners No.2 and 3 are parents and petitioners No.4 and 5 are younger brother and sister of the deceased.

Due to this accident petitioners have lost the bread earner of the family and suffered lot of pain, shock,
mental agony and financial difficulties.

4. The accident occurred due to rash and negligent driving of the driver of the Tempo bearing Reg.No.KA-53/D- 5269, against whom the Whitefield Traffic Police filed criminal case in Cr No.139/2022 for the offences punishable U/Sec.279 and 304(A) of IPC.
5. The Respondent No.1 is being RC owner and Respondent No.2 is being Insurer of the offending vehicle are jointly and severally liable to pay the compensation to the Petitioners.
Hence, the Petitioners pray to grant the compensation.
6. In pursuance to the notice, Respondent No.2 has appeared through its Counsel and filed Written statement.
Respondent No.1 did not appear before the tribunal and hence he was placed exparte.
7. Brief averments of the written statement of Respondent No.2 are that, the petition is not maintainable either in law or on facts of the case.

It is contended that the alleged insured Mahindra Tempo is a goods vehicle and deceased was travelling as gratutious passenger and this respondent has not received any premium to cover the risk of any passenger/Co-driver, except one person who is meant for operation/maintenance of the alleged insured tempo.

It is further contended that the driver of the alleged tempo is not having valid driving licence at the time of accident and it is not having valid permit and fitness certificate and using of the vehicle in a public place without having valid permit and fitness certificate is violation of the terms and condition of the policy and also against to the provisions of the Motor Vehicles Act.

Further it is contended that the petition has been filed by claiming the relationship of employee and employer between the deceased and the respondent No.1, hence, the matter should be adjudicated U/Sec.167 of Motor Vehicle Act 1988.
The insurance policy does not cover the risk of any person travelling in the insured light goods tempo as passengers/coolie's/co-driver, except the driver/owner.
Further, denied the age, income and occupation of the deceased and denied the relationship of deceased with the petitioner.
It is contended that, the compensation amount claimed is highly excessive, exaggerated, arbitrary and speculative.
Hence, prayed to dismiss the petition against this respondent.

8. Based on the above pleadings, this tribunal framed the following:

Whether the Petitioners prove that, on 04.10.2022 at about 1.30 p.m, the deceased (Ram Kumar Gurung) was proceeding as a co-driver in a Mahindra Tempo bearing Reg.No.KA-53/D-5269 and one Sanju Pariyar was driving the same, when reached near Chinnaiah Reddy Compound, Varthur, Bangalore, the driver of the said vehicle drove the same in a rash and negligent manner, so as to endangering to human life,
came at high speed and dashed against the left side of the Chinnaiah Reddy Compound.
As a result of forced impact deceased's head struck between Compound wall and tempo and he sustained several grievous injuries and died on the way to the hospital?

17. The learned counsel for the petitioners argued that the deceased was proceeding in the offending vehicle as a co- driver and due to rash and negligent driving of the offending vehicle the accident took place.
Hence, prayed to award the compensation as prayed.
18. The learned counsel for respondent No.2 argued that, the deceased was not the co-driver and he was travelling as a gratutious passenger.
Hence, the petitioners are not entitled for the compensation.

19. On perusal of Ex.P.1 and 2 the FIR and complaint, it appears that the deceased was inmate of the offending vehicle, on perusal of Ex.P.3 and P.4 the spot mahazar and sketch, it discloses that the accident occurred by dashing to the compound wall on left side of the road and though there is sufficient space for moving the offending vehicle on right side of the said vehicle, the driver of offending vehicle took his vehicle to his left side and dashed to the Wall and caused the accident.

Further on perusal of Ex.P.8 and 9 i.e., notice U/Sec.133 of IMV Act and reply to the said notice, in the reply the owner of the vehicle admitted that one Sanju Pariyar was driving the vehicle on the date of alleged accident and the said driver is having valid D.L. and insurance was in force on the date of accident.
So it clearly indicates that the offending vehicle was involved in the accident.

Further on perusal of charge sheet, it discloses that, the Whitefield Traffic Police filed the case against the driver of Mahindra Tempo bearing Reg.No.KA-53/D-5269 for the offence punishable U/Sec.279 and 304(A) of IPC r/w Sec.134(A&B), 187 of IMV Act.
20.

The Hon'ble Apex Court in the decision reported in 2011 SAR(Civil) 319 Kausum and others V/s Satbir and others held that, in the petition for compensation U/Sec.166 of Motor Vehicles Act.1988 the Petitioners have to prove the incident only on the preponderance of the probabilities and standard of proof beyond all reasonable doubt is not required.

Therefore considering all these aspects this Tribunal come to conclusion that, the said accident occurred due to the rash and negligent driving of the driver of the Mahindra Tempo bearing Reg.No.KA-53/ D-5269.
Accordingly this Tribunal answered Issue No.1 in the affirmative.

27.
The Petitioner No.1 is the wife of deceased, she lost her husband at the age of 27 years.

Regarding consortium, this tribunal has relied upon the decision reported in 2013 ACJ 1403, in which it is held as, "Words and phrases -Consortium - Consortium is the right of spouse to the company, care, help, comfort, guidance, society, solace,
affection and sexual relations with his or her mate".
Hence, it is not possible to compensate the loss of love and affection of the deceased with the Petitioner No.1 by compensating in quantum of amount.

In this regard, the Hon'ble Supreme Court of India passed in 2017 ACJ 2700 SC (between National Insurance co. ltd., V/s Pranay Sethi and others.) held that, Reasonable figures on conventional heads, namely, loss of estate, loss of consortium and funeral expenses should be Rs.15,000/-, Rs.40,000/- and Rs.15,000/- respectively.

sentences.text: The Motor Vehicles Act is a beneficial legislation aimed at providing relief to the victims or their families, in cases of genuine claims.
In case where a parent has lost their minor child, or unmarried son or daughter, the parents are entitled to be awarded loss of consortium under the head of Filial Consortium.
Parental consortium is awarded to children who lose their parents in motor vehicle accidents under the Act.
A few High courts have awarded compensation on this count.
However, there was no clarity with respect to the principles on which compensation could be awarded on loss of Filial Consortium.
The amount of compensation to be awarded as consortium will be governed by the Principles of awarding compensation under "Loss of consortium" as laid down in Pranay Sethi (Supra).
In the present case, we deem it appropriate to award the father and the sister of the deceased, an amount of Rs.40,000/-each, for loss of Filial Consortium.

As per the Petition, the Respondent No.1 is the RC Owner and respondent No.2 is the insurer of the Mahindra Tempo bearing Reg.No.KA-53/D-5269.

sentences.text: RW.1 has stated that, nowhere it is stated that, the deceased was traveling as a co-driver.
Further stated that the deceased was traveling as a co-passenger.
The insured has violated the policy conditions.
The respondent has not collected premium to cover the co-passenger/passenger/co- driver.

In cross-examination he has admitted that in Ex.P.5 the avocation of the deceased was shown as driver.
35.

On perusal of Ex.R.2, the insurance policy of the offending vehicle, it appears that in Col.No.2 of limited as to use: Use for carrying passengers in the vehicles, except employees (other than the driver) not exceeding the number permitted in the registration document are permitted to travel.
On perusal of the insurance copy of the vehicle the registered seating capacity including driver is two.
Therefore, the permitted seating capacity is for 2 persons for the offending vehicle.
As per the say of the petitioners he was travelling as a co-driver in the offending vehicle, but as per the say of respondent No.2 the deceased was travelling as gratutious passenger.
On perusal of Ex.P.5 the inquest panchanama, the avocation of the deceased is shown as driver.
The petitioner No.1 in a re-statement has also stated the avocation of her husband as driver.
The petitioners in their petition has also clearly stated that the deceased was travelling as a co-driver.
The respondent No.2 has not produced any cogent evidence to show that the deceased was traveling as a gratutious passenger.
Except oral evidence of RW.1 there is nothing on record to show that the deceased was traveling as gratutious passenger.
On perusal of insurance policy two persons are permitted to travel in the offending vehicle.
On perusal of entire police records, it appears that, only two persons i.e., the deceased and driver of the offending vehicle were travelling in the offending vehicle at the time of accident.
Hence, it appears that no policy conditions are violated.
Further, on perusal of the entire materials on record, it appears that the deceased was travelling in the offending vehicle as co-driver and not as gratutious passengers.

The learned counsel for the respondent No.2 has relied upon the decisions as follows:

For the foregoing reasons, this Tribunal has proceed to pass the following:-
ORDER
The claim petition filed under Section 166 of the Motor Vehicles Act filed by the Petitioners is hereby Partly allowed with cost.

The petitioners are entitled for total compensation of Rs.35,10,100/- with interest @
6% p.a., from the date of petition till its realization.
The Respondent No.1 and 2 are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation to the Petitioners.
Further, Respondent No.2 being Insurer of the offending vehicle is directed to deposit the compensation amount together with 6% interest within 60 days, from the date of this order.

The Petitioner No.1 is entitled for Rs.15,10,100/-, petitioner No.2 and 4 are entitled for Rs.5,00,000/-each, petitioner No.3 is entitled for Rs.8,00,000/- and petitioner No.5 is entitled for Rs.2,00,000/- with interest.

After deposit, out of awarded share compensation amount 50% each, with interest shall be released in favour of the Petitioner No.1 to 4 and entire share of the petitioner No.5 with proper identification and the remaining their shares with interest shall be deposited in their names in FD in any nationalized bank, for a period of Three years.
Advocate fee is fixed at Rs.1,000/-.
Draw the award accordingly.

opennyai_summary.ANALYSIS:
Hence, prayed to award the compensation as prayed.
The Hon'ble Apex Court in the decision reported in 2011 SAR(Civil) 319 Kausum and others V/s Satbir and others held that, in the petition for compensation U/Sec.166 of Motor Vehicles Act.1988 the Petitioners have to prove the incident only on the preponderance of the probabilities and standard of proof beyond all reasonable doubt is not required.

"In case the deceased was self employed or on a fixed salary, an addition of 40% of the established income should be the warrant where the deceased was below the age of 40 year.
Hence, the Petitioners are considered as dependents on the income of deceased.
So, relying upon the decision reported in 2009 ACJ 1298 (Sarla Varma and others - Vs- Delhi Transport Corporation & another), out of the salary of the deceased 1/4th has to be deducted towards the personal expenses of the deceased.
In this regard the Hon'ble Supreme Court of India was held in the case of Magma General Insurance Co. ltd., V/s Nanu Ram @
Chuhru Ram & Ors., (Civil Appeal No.9581/2018 (Arising out of SLP (civil) 3192/2018)
The Motor Vehicles Act is a beneficial legislation aimed at providing relief to the victims or their families, in cases of genuine claims.
In case where a parent has lost their minor child, or unmarried son or daughter, the parents are entitled to be awarded loss of consortium under the head of Filial Consortium.
Parental consortium is awarded to children who lose their parents in motor vehicle accidents under the Act.
The amount of compensation to be awarded as consortium will be governed by the Principles of awarding compensation under "Loss of consortium" as laid down in Pranay Sethi (Supra).

The insured has violated the policy conditions.
On perusal of Ex.P.5 the inquest panchanama, the avocation of the deceased is shown as driver.
The respondent No.2 has not produced any cogent evidence to show that the deceased was traveling as a gratutious passenger.
Except oral evidence of RW.1 there is nothing on record to show that the deceased was traveling as gratutious passenger.
On perusal of insurance policy two persons are permitted to travel in the offending vehicle.
On perusal of entire police records, it appears that, only two persons i.e., the deceased and driver of the offending vehicle were travelling in the offending vehicle at the time of accident.
Hence, it appears that no policy conditions are violated.
Further, on perusal of the entire materials on record, it appears that the deceased was travelling in the offending vehicle as co-driver and not as gratutious passengers.

ORDER
The claim petition filed under Section 166 of the Motor Vehicles Act filed by the Petitioners is hereby Partly allowed with cost.
